Names are less easily fully taken in Ferrytown than rumors and tall tales would have you believe. Due to the influence of the material plane, the casual giving of one's name to a fey often won't cause any negative effects for the giver, though the fey will gain. However, in select cases involving powerful magic, one may give away the whole and entirety of one's name. If this is done, the following things will happen.
1: the character's name in the server nickname will be changed to 'The Nameless', 'Nameless one', or similar.
2: No one will be allowed to refer to the character by their former name. Flavor-wise, anyone who tries to will feel a profound sense of wrongness and resistance when they try. if they do so anyway, they take 1d6 psychic damage (which may be escalated at DM discretion.) 
3: Similarly, the character may not be referred to by any unique name until they have earned a new one. They may be referred to by any earned titles or things like 'dude', 'fam', 'buddy', etc., not may not be given a unique nickname or chosen name until the DM who took the name in the first place determines the character has earned a new one. This new name will be entirely up to the player.
4: The player feels a profound sense of disconnectedness from themself until they earn a new name. For that duration, they suffer disadvantage on any mental (int, wis, and cha) saving throws and may struggle to have a sense of identity. In most cases they will retain their memories, though they may feel like someone else's until they earn a new name.
5: NPCs who have interacted with the player previously may forget them or struggle to remember them. fey will be aware of why this is, but non-fey may not.
